fields.text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the three branches of the Philippine government are:
fields.explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art. VI, Sec. 1), executive power in the President (Art. VII, Sec. 1), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
fields.hint: Think of who makes the laws, who carries them out, and who interprets them.
fields.whyB: Elections are run by the COMELEC, a constitutional commission, not a separate branch of government.
fields.whyC: The Constitutional Commissions (Art. IX) are independent bodies, not one of the three branches; the Executive is missing.
fields.whyD: Local governments (Art. X) are political subdivisions, not a branch; the Legislative is missing.
fields.explanationTl: Sa 1987 Constitution, ang legislative power ay nasa Congress (Art. VI, Sec. 1), ang executive power ay nasa President (Art. VII, Sec. 1), at ang judicial power ay nasa Supreme Court at lower courts (Art. VIII, Sec. 1). Kaya tatlo: Executive, Legislative, Judicial.
fields.hintTl: Isipin mo: sino ang gumagawa ng batas, sino ang nagpapatupad, at sino ang nag-i-interpret?

fields.text: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity through which effect?
fields.explanation: Solar cells use the photovoltaic effect: light striking a semiconductor such as silicon frees electrons and produces an electric current.
fields.hint: The name joins the Greek word for light with the unit of electric potential.
fields.whyA: The greenhouse effect is the trapping of heat by gases in the atmosphere; it does not generate electricity.
fields.whyC: The piezoelectric effect produces electricity from mechanical pressure, not from light.
fields.whyD: The Doppler effect is the change in frequency of a wave from a moving source; it has nothing to do with electricity.
fields.explanationTl: Photovoltaic effect ang ginagamit ng solar cells: pag tinamaan ng liwanag ang semiconductor tulad ng silicon, may electrons na nare-release at nagkakaroon ng electric current.
fields.hintTl: Pinagsama sa pangalan ang Greek word para sa 'light' at ang unit ng electric potential.

fields.text: In oxy-fuel welding and cutting, which gas is commonly burned with oxygen as the fuel?
fields.explanation: Acetylene burned with pure oxygen gives the hottest common fuel-gas flame (over 3,000 °C), hot enough to melt steel, so it is the standard fuel in oxy-fuel welding.
fields.hint: Only one option is a gas that can burn.
fields.whyA: Nitrogen does not burn; it is mostly inert and is used for purging, not as a fuel.
fields.whyC: Argon is an inert shielding gas used in TIG and MIG welding; it cannot burn.
fields.whyD: Carbon dioxide is a shielding gas in MIG welding; it is already fully burned and cannot be a fuel.
fields.explanationTl: Acetylene ang fuel gas sa oxy-fuel welding. Pag sinunog ito kasama ng pure oxygen, umaabot sa mahigit 3,000 °C ang flame, sapat para matunaw ang steel.
fields.hintTl: Isa lang sa mga choices ang gas na nasusunog.

fields.text: Philippine Independence Day is celebrated every:
fields.explanation: Independence Day marks the proclamation of Philippine independence from Spain by Emilio Aguinaldo in Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898. The celebration was moved from July 4 to June 12 in 1962 and fixed by Republic Act No. 4166 (1964).
fields.hint: Think of the 1898 proclamation in Kawit, Cavite.
fields.whyB: July 4 is when the US recognized Philippine independence in 1946; it was celebrated as Independence Day only until 1961 and was renamed Republic Day.
fields.whyC: August 31 is not Philippine Independence Day; National Heroes Day falls on the last Monday of August.
fields.whyD: April 9 is Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valor), commemorating the Fall of Bataan in 1942.
fields.explanationTl: June 12 ang Independence Day natin, kasi noong June 12, 1898 dineklara ni Emilio Aguinaldo ang independence mula sa Spain sa Kawit, Cavite. Dati July 4 ang celebration, pero inilipat sa June 12 noong 1962 at ginawang batas ng RA 4166 noong 1964.
fields.hintTl: Alalahanin mo ang proclamation sa Kawit, Cavite noong 1898.
